issues.description: The problem statement is internally inconsistent about the nature of the SealSaloon.stock attribute. Earlier it instructs the saloon to have a "final Stock stock" (implying an instance final field initialized in the constructor), while a later note explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static (shared across all instances). The provided solution implements stock as a static final field. This contradiction can confuse students whether to implement stock as an instance final field or as a static class-level field, which affects how they must write acceptSupplyDelivery and calculateTotalPrice (both required to be static).
issues.suggested_fix: Make the requirement for the stock attribute consistent. Either: (A) Update the problem statement and UML to state that stock is a static final (class-level) field shared across all SealSaloon instances and ensure related instructions (e.g., make getStock() static) reflect that; or (B) remove the 'must be static' note and require an instance final Stock field initialized in the constructor (and update the requirements for acceptSupplyDelivery and calculateTotalPrice to be instance methods). Prefer option A if the intention is to have a shared stock (matches the solution).
